chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What is your view regarding a man who struck a young woman on her stomach, injuring her womb and disrupting her menstruation, and she stated that her menstruation had ceased because of that, while her menstruation had previously been regular? He said: “She is to be observed for a year. If her menstruation returns to what it was, otherwise she is made to swear an oath, and the one who struck her is fined one-third of her indemnity for the damage to her womb and the cessation of her menstruation.”

key_terms.ثُلُثَ دِيَتِهَا: one-third of her indemnity; the financial compensation imposed
key_terms.رَحِمَهَا: her womb; the organ harmed by the assault
key_terms.سَنَةً: one year; the duration set to determine whether the condition is permanent
key_terms.طَمْثُهَا: her menstruation; the monthly bleeding whose cessation is under discussion
key_terms.فَسَادِ رَحِمِهَا: damage to her womb; the physical injury requiring compensation
key_terms.يُنْتَظَرُ: she is to be waited upon or observed; indicating a period of legal observation
key_terms.ٱرْتِفَاعِ طَمْثِهَا: the cessation of her menstruation; the loss resulting from the injury
key_terms.ٱسْتُحْلِفَتْ: she is made to swear an oath; a legal oath used to establish the claim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man injures a woman and her menstruation stops as a result?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury to a woman that causes harm to her womb and the cessation of menstruation. Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام rules that the case should be observed for one year, and if the condition persists and is confirmed by oath, the assailant must pay one-third of her diyah as compensation.
